4 أَكْنَبَتْ يَدُهُ ; and ↓ كَنِبَتْ , aor.
كَنَبَ , inf. n. كَنَبٌ; (K;) or the former verb only is used; not the latter; (As, S;) His hand was, or became, callous, or hard, (S,) or coarse, or rough, (K,) by reason of work. (S, K.) See 1. ―
-b2- اكنب لِسَانُهُ His tongue was impeded, or tied up.
(K.) ―
-b3- اكنب عَلَيْهِ بَطْنُهُ His belly [meaning its contents] oppressed him, or gave him pain: syn. إِشْتَدَّ. (K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
